policy: A trustworthy government-published consolidated text or clearly identified official page may be accepted as an external reference within its displayed identity, status, version, language, date and subject. If authority, version or content is unclear, offer the whole official website/service for human review. A reviewed official link is sufficient for ordinary source use; a local copy, custom retrieval/conversion rule, API, full Gazette-chain reconstruction, hash, replay or scheduled update is not a blanket prerequisite. External-link acceptance is separate from local-copy acceptance, topic coverage and country review completion.

publisher_assessment.decision: Likumi.lv is accepted as a trustworthy official publisher-managed source of consolidated legislation for ordinary reference use within each page’s displayed version and status. The official portal says the Latvijas Vēstnesis publisher maintains it, provides current/historical/future versions and validity status, and that the content is informational with the official Gazette prevailing in a discrepancy.
publisher_assessment.basis: The official Likumi.lv About page and Act record identify the public legal-text service and publisher; the new EU-family Act record displays its issuer, current status, commencement date and official Gazette publication. Latvijas Vēstnesis provides the publication record and OP identifier.
publisher_assessment.limits: Latvian is the controlling text for the new free-movement Act; the official English record says it has not been translated by the State Language Centre. A legal link does not confirm every linked operational instruction or establish coverage completeness.
publisher_assessment.local_copy_and_reuse: Thirty selected local text copies have been accepted in their recorded per-source scope after official identity/version review and deterministic replay. Four accepted references remain link-only navigation or homepage routes; thirteen converted candidate texts remain archived but unaccepted (five pending references, four not-relied-upon records, and four link-only navigation/homepage copies). The OP 2026/119.1 original PDF is stored with its reviewed text extraction; the old PMLP PDF (lv-22) remains unaccepted in the Monitor archive. Publisher reuse terms concern recurring retention/retrieval, not ordinary linking. No scheduled updater is proposed by this local-copy review.

currentness_and_dependency_note: The new free-movement Act took effect on 10 July 2026 and sets 1 December 2027 deadlines for specified Cabinet regulations. Its transitional text says applications filed before commencement are handled under Regulation 675. The official Regulation 675 record, however, says it remains in force until 2 December 2027. This review records the regulation as an official legal reference but leaves its applicability to applications filed on or after 10 July 2026 unresolved; the stale MFA guidance is not used to resolve that conflict. The new Immigration Law is a separate third-country regime effective 15 September 2026; certain provisions take effect on 31 December 2027. Issue-led discovery also added the Residence Declaration Act, Register of Natural Persons Act (selected edition from 29 April 2026), and Civil Status Act as current official references for address registration, population-register records, and civil-status evidence. They do not resolve local implementation or all foreign-document recognition questions.
